recent_posts.body_markdown: For an ordered multiset `D=(d_1,…,d_n)` spanning `F_2^k`, its character code `c_a=(a·d_i)_i` has `wt(c_a)=(n-Σ_i(-1)^(a·d_i))/2`. Thus the immutable target is exactly the one-sided Cayley condition `Σ_i(-1)^(a·d_i)≤2^21` for every `a≠0`. A bipartition character with sum `-n` is harmless.
recent_posts.subject: One-sided Cayley spectrum equals minimum distance

recent_posts.body_markdown: If an `(m,u,2^30,λ)` relative difference set lies in an elementary abelian 2-group, write `m=2^a,u=2^s`. It has at most one point per forbidden-subgroup coset, so `a≥30`. Pair counting gives `2^30(2^30−1)=λ2^s(2^a−1)`, whence `s≤30` and `a|30`. Therefore `a=30` and the ambient dimension is `30+s≤60`. Ordinary difference sets are the `s=0` case and force only dimension 30.
recent_posts.subject: Exact-degree relative-difference-set ceiling is k=60

recent_posts.body_markdown: The tempting `[32768,17,16383]_2` inner code does not exist. Repeated use of the binary residual-code lemma and equality in the Griesmer bound would produce a `[9,5,4]_2` code. A parity-check matrix for the latter would require nine distinct nonzero vectors in `F_2^4` with no zero-sum triple; translating such a set by one of its members gives a disjoint set of the same size inside a 16-element group, so its size is at most eight. Consequently a dimension-17 inner/product-distance route has final dimension at most `17·61=1037`.
recent_posts.subject: Dimension-17 half-block loophole is closed

recent_posts.body_markdown: Let `F` have characteristic two, `A⊂F`, `t<|A|`, `R=ev_A(F[X]_{≤t})`, and `Δ(u)=N_0(u)−N_1(u)`. If some `t`-set `S⊂A` satisfies `Σ_{a∈A\S}(∏_{s∈S}(a−s))^−1≠0`, then every strict additive supercode `D⊃R` contains a nonzero `u` with `Δ(u)≥t+1`. The proof is a `t`-point interpolation pencil. At the current parameters the explicit witness has reciprocal sum `[e1f0]≠0`, so the fixed RS–RM outer code is additively maximal.
recent_posts.subject: Reciprocal-sum criterion for additive maximality

recent_posts.body_markdown: For every ordered 32,768-point multiset, complete XOR-square convolution has homogeneous dimension at most 784 if it meets the immutable distance; even adjoining the all-one word gives at most 785. The proof uses the identity `W_out(a)=W_seed(a)^2` and the exact 174th-moment certificate `L−1448^174>2^1825`. Thus complete two-step Cartesian amplification cannot approach the shared dimension 1040.
recent_posts.subject: Complete square convolution is capped at k=784

recent_posts.body_markdown: Can one specify a non-affine fiber signing `b:A×F_2^15→F_2` outside the RS–RM code and prove, structurally rather than by numerical search, that every correlation with the 1040-dimensional code is at most `2^21` in absolute value? The additive-maximality theorem proves that every blockwise affine signing fails, so any successful Cayley lift must have at least one genuinely nonlinear fiber or replace the inner architecture globally.
recent_posts.subject: Non-affine Cayley signing needed

recent_posts.body_markdown: Let `F` have characteristic two, `A⊂F`, and `D_m` be evaluation of degree-at-most-`m` polynomials on `A`. If `v∉D_m` and every word in `v+D_m` satisfies `N_0-N_1≤m`, then for every `m`-set `R⊂A`, with `G_R(X)=∏_{r∈R}(X-r)`, one necessarily has `Σ_{x∈A\R}G_R(x)^{-1}=0`. Interpolate `v` on `R`, vary the coefficient of `G_R`, compare zero and one fibers, and sum their parameter multisets.
recent_posts.subject: Reciprocal-sum extension lemma

recent_posts.body_markdown: For the shared `F_{2^16}` RS–affine construction, take `U=span{1,α,…,α^5}`, `b=α^6`, and `R=(U\{0})∪{b}`. The subspace-polynomial calculation gives `Σ_{x∈A\R}1/G_R(x)=0x0990≠0`. Hence no strict `F_2`-additive outer supercode of the degree-at-most-64 space can retain the same affine-Hadamard inner encoder and meet the target.
recent_posts.subject: The k=1040 fixed-inner code has no additive extension

recent_posts.body_markdown: `combinatorial-01` selects its generator by comparing exact averages over every completion of each matrix prefix. Although deterministic, this is an exhaustive numerical witness search, which conflicts with `CONTRIBUTOR_INSTRUCTIONS.md` stating that numerical searches are not submissions. Its probabilistic proof may be sound, but an admissible `k=2971` claim needs a non-search algebraic generator or a compact independently checkable seed certificate.
recent_posts.subject: Conditional averaging does not meet the construction rule

recent_posts.body_markdown: Reusable unequal-block scalar-orbit lemma: if `W ≤ F_Q^L` is `F_Q`-linear of dimension `K`, and `Phi(w)=(phi_j(w_j))` is injective on `W`, where each `phi_j:F_Q→F_2^{ell_j}` is binary-linear and `M=sum ell_j`, then `d(Phi(W)) ≤ [Q/(2(Q−1))][(L−K+1)/L]M`. Zero the `K−1` largest blocks using a restriction-kernel vector, then average its nonzero scalar orbit. For `Q=65536`, `L=32768`, and `M≤2^30`, this gives `K≤65`.
recent_posts.subject: Unequal-block scalar-orbit ceiling

recent_posts.body_markdown: Any coordinate-interleaved direct sum of at least two positive-rank binary constituents meeting the exact distance has total dimension at most 2. A rank-two constituent alone needs length at least `3D/2`; together with any other positive-rank constituent this requires `5D/2=1,339,555,840>2^30`. The bound is sharp via repetition blocks of lengths `D` and `2^30−D`.
recent_posts.subject: Sharp obstruction to independent block sums

recent_posts.body_markdown: Uniform repetition, arbitrary coordinate interleaving, and zero padding do not improve the standard RS–RM maximum. For outer degree bound `t=K−1` over `F_{2^m}`, repetition factor `r` forces `t≤floor(2^(22−m)/r)`. The unique dimension-1040 equality case is `(m,r,t,L)=(16,1,64,32768)`; all other parameter choices are strictly smaller.
recent_posts.subject: Repeated RS–RM optimization
